Flatbed Truck.definition: A truck with a completely FLAT, OPEN rear bed. KEY FEATURES: 1) NO side walls at all (the bed is fully open on the sides), 2) NO large curved/arched front bulkhead behind the cab - may only have a simple FLAT headache rack (small vertical panel) or nothing at all, 3) NO dump capability. CRITICAL: If you see a LARGE, PROMINENT curved/arched structure behind the cab that bends forward over it, it is NOT a Flatbed Truck - it is a Flatbed Dump. Simple flat headache rack = Flatbed Truck. Large curved bulkhead = Flatbed Dump.

Pickup Truck.definition: A light-duty truck with an open cargo bed, typically integrated with the cab or a separate, fixed bed. It does NOT have enclosed service compartments forming the main body, nor is it a dedicated dump body.

Mechanics Truck.definition: A service body truck with a visible crane attached. The crane is the key differentiator from a standard Utility Truck - Service Truck. Always overrides Utility Truck classification.

Utility Truck - Service Truck.definition: A specialized type of Utility/Service Truck. Its DEFINING feature is a large, prominent ladder or material rack mounted over the service body, designed to carry long items like pipes, lumber, or ladders. The presence of this rack is the key identifier.

Dump Truck.definition: A heavy-duty truck with an ENCLOSED CARGO BOX formed by SOLID SIDE WALLS. VISUAL IDENTIFICATION: 1) You CANNOT see the bed surface from the side - it is HIDDEN behind solid metal walls, 2) SOLID VERTICAL METAL PANELS run along the LEFT and RIGHT sides of the cargo area, creating a BOX/CONTAINER, 3) Side walls are TALL - equal to or TALLER than the cab height, 4) The cargo area looks like an enclosed BOX, NOT a flat open platform. CRITICAL DISTINCTION FROM FLATBED DUMP: If you can see the flat bed surface from the side (no side walls blocking the view) = NOT a Dump Truck, it's a Flatbed Dump!

Flatbed Dump.definition: A truck with a FLAT, OPEN bed (NO side walls) and a LARGE CURVED bulkhead behind the cab. VISUAL IDENTIFICATION: 1) The bed is FLAT and OPEN - you can see the bed surface from the side (often aluminum or steel platform), NO solid walls on the sides, 2) Behind the cab is a LARGE, PROMINENT curved/arched structure (often black/dark) that bends forward over the cab like a shed-like arc, 3) This is NOT a Dump Truck because there are NO SIDE WALLS - the bed is exposed and open. CRITICAL: If you see a flat bed surface visible from the side + curved bulkhead behind cab = FLATBED DUMP, not Dump Truck!

Landscape Truck.definition: A dump truck with SHORT/LOW side walls designed for landscaping materials. KEY FEATURES: 1) Side walls ARE present but are SHORT - clearly LOWER than the cab/driver compartment height, 2) Curved/arched front bulkhead present behind cab (like Dump Truck), 3) Used for soil, mulch, debris. CRITICAL HEIGHT TEST: If carrier/box height is LESS than cab height = Landscape Truck. If carrier/box height is EQUAL or GREATER than cab height = Dump Truck.

Contractor Truck.definition: A truck that requires ALL three components: toolboxes + stakebed + ladder rack. This is a very specific combination.

Stake Bed.definition: A Flatbed Truck with tall removable stake sides, NO permanent toolboxes, NO fold-down gates (distinguishes from Flatbed Dump).

Hauler.definition: A truck with any visible gooseneck hitch or bed cutout, designed for hauling trailers or heavy equipment.

Cab Chassis.definition: A truck with No bed or box installed (no flatbed, dump, box, etc. of any kind). The rear frame rails, suspension, or fuel tank must be clearly visible behind the cab, with no installed body.

Stepvan.definition: A walk-in delivery van (UPS/FedEx style), typically with a distinct upright driver position and cargo area accessible from the cab.

Selfloader.definition: A specialized tow truck with wheel-lift claws (no ramp or flatbed) for loading vehicles.

Bucket Truck - Boom Truck.definition: A truck with a hydraulic boom + bucket attached for aerial work. Always overrides Utility Truck classification.

Cabover Truck - COE.definition: A truck where the driver sits ABOVE the engine. The cab is positioned directly over the engine, giving the truck a flat front appearance. Also known as Cab Over Engine (COE).

Box Truck - Straight Truck.definition: A truck with a large rectangular cargo box attached to the cab. The box is a fully enclosed cargo area. ALWAYS check for Moving Van features (slide-out ramp or liftgate).

Moving Van.definition: A Box Truck or Straight Truck that has a visible SLIDE-OUT RAMP or a LIFTGATE mechanism at the rear, designed for moving personal belongings.

Refrigerated Truck.definition: A truck with a visible refrigeration unit above the cab, designed for transporting temperature-sensitive cargo. Mutually exclusive with Box Truck if primary classification.

Cutaway Cube Van.definition: SECONDARY CATEGORY ONLY - describes a Box Truck built on a van chassis (Ford E-Series, Chevrolet Express, etc.) with a visible pass-through door/opening from the cab to the cargo box. MUST ALWAYS be paired with 'Box Truck - Straight Truck' as the PRIMARY category. Never output alone. The pass-through door allowing driver access to cargo area is the KEY identifier.

Van.definition: A general van classification without specific body type modifiers.

Cargo Van.definition: A van designed primarily for hauling cargo rather than passengers. Features an enclosed cargo area.

Passanger Van.definition: A van designed primarily for transporting passengers, with seating capacity beyond the front row.

Rollback - Tow Truck.definition: A tow truck with a sliding/inclining flatbed for vehicle transport. The bed can tilt and slide back to load vehicles.

Conventional Day Cab.definition: A large hood + no sleeper + tractor-style truck configuration where the driver sits behind the engine. Must have visible chassis frame or hitch behind cab. Cannot be combined with other truck bodies except Cab Chassis.

Dually.definition: A vehicle with DUAL REAR WHEELS - characterized by 4 REAR TIRES instead of 2 (2 tires on each side of rear axle). This allows the vehicle to carry more weight. Rear fenders BULGE OUT significantly wider than front fenders.

Dry Van.definition: Almost identical to a Box Truck, but should only be assigned to larger models where the box is 20’+
